headline: I tried to follow the government’s new 'Polite Self-Departure' guidelines and ended up living in my car in the driveway
body:
I am a simple man who believes in following instructions, which is why I was genuinely touched when the administration sent me a friendly pamphlet titled 'Your Voluntary Path Out.' It suggested that the most patriotic thing a resident could do is leave their own house of their own volition. Being a rule-abider, I immediately packed my entire living room into the trunk, placed a 'See you later, maybe' note on the kitchen table, and drove my car exactly six inches forward to the end of the driveway.

Living in my hatchback for the last three weeks has been an exercise in civic duty, though the neighbors are starting to ask questions. I spend my mornings sitting on the roof of the car, waving politely at my own front door as if I were a visitor passing through a foreign land. I even tried to serve myself an eviction notice, but it felt awkward given that I’m the one who pays the mortgage. 

I’ve reached out to the local department of voluntary exits to see if I am being polite enough in my departure, but they just tell me I’m still 'technically within the zip code.' They suggested I move to the sidewalk next, which seems like a reasonable compromise. I’m currently looking for a good folding chair; if I’m going to be a displaced person, I at least want to ensure I’m not blocking the mailman's route.
caption: When the government asks nicely for you to leave your own home, the only civilized response is to pack the sedan and move to the curb. My new life as a driveway nomad is going great. (satire) #CivicDuty #SelfDeparture #SuburbanLife
igHook: Would you move to the driveway if your local council sent you a polite invitation to leave?
imagePrompt: A nondescript suburban house with a driveway featuring a small, packed sedan parked precariously at the very edge of the property line, with an open car door visible.

sourceHeadline.title: 'Get off our roads Mr Singh': Trump administration's 'self-deport' advertisement sparks row
